long_biography.plain_text:
Eric Smidt entered the family tool business as a teenager, helping his father turn a small Southern California telephone-sales operation into Harbor Freight Tools. The pair shifted towards mail order, while Smidt developed a direct-factory sourcing model that removed intermediaries and lowered prices. He became president, later bought his father's stake and continued as owner and chief executive.

That ownership structure allowed Smidt to guide Harbor Freight's expansion while preserving its focus on tools for tradespeople and home users. Education became a connected civic chapter through Harbor Freight Tools for Schools, the flagship programme of his foundation. It supports skilled-trades teaching in American public high schools, linking the business he built with practical routes into welding, automotive work, construction and other skilled careers.
